tool_plan.objective: Generate and preserve representative Chromium web-cache content for ChromeCacheView inspection, including cacheable document and resource responses.

required_actions.name: browser.launch
required_actions.why: Creates the Chromium session and profile that contains the cache source.

required_actions.name: browser.get_clickables
required_actions.why: Observes available controls and finite options before exercising cache-generating interactions.

required_actions.name: browser.goto
required_actions.why: Loads distinct web documents and their cacheable network resources.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_type
required_actions.why: Supplies a realistic query and can commit a search-driven document transition.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_click
required_actions.why: Exercises visible links or results that load materially different cached content.

required_actions.name: browser.select_option
required_actions.why: Varies observed finite page parameters when they can produce different responses.

required_actions.name: browser.scroll
required_actions.why: Reveals lazy-loaded content and associated cacheable resources.

required_actions.name: browser.close
required_actions.why: Closes the session after interaction so pending browser cache data can be flushed.

completion.detail: Complete after all required actions have been performed in a live Chromium session, including browser.close to flush the cache.

tool_plan.action_intent_guidance: Action Flow: Launch Chromium, then use browser.goto with relevant run-provided runtime resources to load a few distinct, naturally resource-rich pages that visibly acquire cacheable documents, images, scripts, styles, and media. On each suitable page, use browser.get_clickables to inspect currently visible controls and finite choices. Use browser.smart_type where a visible search or text-entry workflow supports a realistic query and transition to a different document, then use browser.smart_click on visible results or links that lead to materially different content. Where observed finite options can change the response, use browser.select_option. Use browser.scroll to reveal lazy-loaded page content and resources, then re-run browser.get_clickables after revealed content when useful; keep this observe -> reveal -> re-observe loop bounded. Close the browser only after these interactions so cache data is flushed for inspection. Artifact focus: page navigations generate cached document and supporting-resource responses; search, link transitions, option changes, and lazy loading broaden the Chromium cache content.
